chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Imran narrated to me from his father Imran ibn Ismail. He said: Abu Ali al-Ansari narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Tamimi. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said:

While Ibrahim, the Friend of the Merciful (peace be upon him), was on the mountain of Bayt al-Maqdis seeking a pasture for his sheep, he suddenly heard a voice and found a man standing in prayer who was twelve cubits tall. He said to him: 'O servant of God! Who do you pray to?' He said: 'To the God of heaven.' So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Is there anyone remaining from your people besides you?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'So from where do you eat?' He said: 'I collect from this tree in the summer and eat it in the winter.' He said to him: 'Where is your dwelling?' So he pointed with his hand toward a mountain.

So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Would you take me with you so that I may spend the night at your place?' He said: 'Before me is water that cannot be waded through.' He said: 'How do you manage?' He said: 'I walk on it.' He said: 'Then take me with you, for perhaps God will grant me what He has granted you.' So the worshipper took him by the hand and they went together until they reached the water, and he walked and Ibrahim (peace be upon him) walked with him until they reached his dwelling. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Which is the greatest of days?' The worshipper said to him: 'The Day of Religion — the day on which people demand recompense from one another.' He said: 'Would you raise your hand and I raise mine, and we supplicate to God Almighty to protect us from the evil of that day?'

He said: 'And what will my supplication avail? By God, I have had a supplication for thirty years that has not been answered at all.' So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Shall I not tell you why your supplication has been withheld?' He said: 'Of course.' He said to him: 'When God Almighty loves a servant, He withholds his supplication so that he may continue to whisper to Him, ask Him, and seek from Him. And when He hates a servant, He hastens the granting of his supplication, or He casts despair of it into his heart.' Then he said to him: 'And what was your supplication?'

He said: 'A shepherd passed by me with a boy who had a lock of hair. So I said: O boy! Whose are these sheep? He said: They belong to Ibrahim, the Friend of the Merciful. So I said: O God! If You have a Friend on earth, then show him to me.' So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him: 'God has answered your supplication. I am Ibrahim, the Friend of the Merciful.' So he embraced him. When God sent Muhammad (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), the handshake came.

key_terms.احْتِبَاسُ الدَّعْوَةِ: Withholding of supplication — a theological concept explaining why God delays answering the prayers of His beloved servants
key_terms.الْمُصَافَحَةُ: Handshake — the practice of handshaking as a greeting, said to have been instituted with the advent of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), replacing the embrace
key_terms.خَلِيلُ الرَّحْمَنِ: Friend of the Merciful — the Quranic epithet for the Prophet Ibrahim (AS), emphasizing the unique bond of divine friendship (khulla)
key_terms.يَوْمُ الدِّينِ: The Day of Religion/Recompense — an epithet for the Day of Judgment used in Quran 1:4, 82:17-19

ai.seo_question: Why does God withhold the supplications of His beloved servants according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that Ibrahim the Friend of the Merciful encountered a solitary worshipper twelve cubits tall on the mountain of Bayt al-Maqdis. After demonstrating miraculous qualities (walking on water, sustained by seasonal fruit), the worshipper revealed his thirty-year unanswered supplication. Ibrahim explained that God withholds the supplication of His beloved so they continue in intimate dialogue with Him, while hastening the supplication of those He dislikes. This hadith was transmitted through a chain connecting Imam al-Sadiq to Shaykh al-Saduq, who narrated it in his Amali assembled in 368 AH.

so that he may whisper to Him/confide in Him
